key_insight: Test-time LLM ensembling has two distinct data bottlenecks—labeled questions Q and per-question generations N—and the paper shows buffered ERM is near-optimal in many regimes, with excess risk scaling like Q^{-1/2}+N^{-β/2} up to logs.
engineering_relevance: For systems that combine multiple LLMs at inference time, the results give a principled way to budget annotation versus sampling effort and predict when more generations or more labeled questions will actually improve ensemble quality.
method: Buffered ERM with a calibrated margin buffer for weighted model selection.
Minimax analysis of a two-model/two-answer subproblem via Hellinger modulus for a binomial-mixture experiment.
Polynomial approximation and spectral analysis to separate learning regimes in Q and N.
evidence_signal: The paper derives theoretical excess-risk rates and minimax lower bounds, using a simplified submodel to validate when the buffered ERM upper bound is tight up to logarithmic factors.
watch_item: The sharp transitions between regimes and a matching pooled estimator for general ensembles remain unresolved, so practical gains may depend on problem structure.
paper_title: Two Sample Sizes in Test-Time LLM Ensembling: Buffered ERM and Minimax Theory
